title: Production script (version 1, D-43): one file is the script, the voice direction, the picture plan, the sound plan and the edit
description: Written segment by segment: a segment's lines, its shots (with their picture prompts) and its sounds are written together. Times are never written by hand: explainer_engine.production.timing fills them from the read (words.json) into a separate timed file.

schema.description: /2 (2026-10-19): every line carries its visual beats (VB rules, PV-39 FAIL); /3 (2026-10-19, the scene rewrite): dialogue lives in scenes (segments[].scene, lines[].to, SC rules PV-48), cues are opt-in and event-bound (VB-08/VB-10/VB-11); /1 is the legacy contract

gemini_exception.description: the creator's recorded exception letting Gemini paint this episode's own pictures (D-44 style); without it a Gemini paint plan FAILs PP-05

distinct.description: what makes this episode its own (PV-38): compared with docs/episodes.json

rulebook.description: episode_rules.json next to the script (D-51); new-style scripts set it and PV-39..PV-42 apply

scenario.description: PV-45, OR-15: the short scenario the creator approved before this script was written (file next to the script, sha256 binds the approval)

style.description: how the narrator sounds, in descriptive words only (never a real person's name: no imitation, no cloning)

world.description: the world spec read by world.resolver.resolve (host, visitors, light owner, day_arc)

style_refs.description: picture ids that carry the channel look (Gemini frames)

environment.description: the creator's pick from ONE variant collage (OR-16, PV-47): the chosen tile becomes the reference

cast.description: named heroes: how the narration names them, how a picture draws them, what they own

voice.description: the hero's own voice for spoken dialogue lines (D-45): a description of the sound, never a real person to imitate (PV-10, PV-32)

traits.description: VC rules: the character's audible traits (age, gender, temperament, energy, origin), from which audio/casting.py builds the voice search; for a real person only documented traits, never an imitation

ethnicity.description: VC-05: the hero's ethnic or national background, from which the accent is read when origin names none (a Japanese businessman speaks English with a Japanese accent)

documented.description: sourced facts about a real person's speech (era, origin, temperament); claim ids or URLs

expressions.description: VB-06: expression -> a cut-out face/pose PNG of this hero (the face inset swaps it on every change)

face_sheet.description: VB-09: one sheet of close-up expressions on chroma green, painted once from the hero's reference picture and reused in every scene and episode (production/faces.py)

speech.description: PV-46, DW-11: how the hero talks - from their generally known manner (public, with sources) or, for an invented hero, their personality; our own words, never a quote or an actor's delivery

reference.description: the creator's pick from ONE variant collage (OR-16, PV-47): the chosen tile becomes the reference

forbidden_props.description: objects that must never be shown (a magnifier when the story's lens is reading glasses)

library.description: pictures that already exist (made in an earlier version): id -> picture

sound_dirs.description: folders (relative to the script) with sounds by name

picture_dirs.description: folders (relative to the script) with the pictures' files

text.description: exactly what is said, no tags

tags.description: ElevenLabs delivery tags placed before the line

emphasis.description: the one word that carries the surprise (spoken in capitals)

pause_after.description: a held pause after the line in seconds, written as [pause] / ... for the voice and enforced by pause_pad

speaker.description: cast id of the hero who speaks this line in their own voice (D-45, PV-32); absent = the narrator

to.description: SC-04 (/3): who this line is said to - a cast id of scene.present, 'self' or 'room'; a hero never talks to the narrator

intent.description: what the line DOES in the exchange (DW-05/DW-12); a reveal expects another character's reaction

kind.description: Narrative classification for the editorial gate; fact, analysis and speculation require claim references.

visual_beats.description: VB rules: the visual beats of this line (stage 2b, beat-writer), in the order they land

at.description: the words of this segment where the picture appears; the cut goes in the pause before them

reuse.description: SR-08 plan: 'unique' or 'reuse' (the picture appeared before; a different crop, zoom or bubble)

accents.description: MO rules: drawn motion accents on top of the camera move, rendered by production/accents.py

at.description: the words the accent lands on (default: the shot's start)

text.description: pop_text / slam_text: the words shown (at most 4)

purpose.description: why this picture is on screen now (PV-42 REVIEW when missing)

cut.description: why the cut or transition into this shot suits the beat (the type stays in transition/UR-14)

purpose.description: the event's narrative or emotional job (PV-41)

beds.description: ambience changes inside the segment, each from its phrase until the next change (crossfaded); a story sound starts on its event's words

purpose.description: the event's narrative or emotional job (PV-41)

period.description: the time-jump chapter this segment belongs to (day1, week1, month1, year1, year10, year100, compare)

scene.description: SC rules (docs/STORY_ENGINE.md, PV-48): the staged scene this segment's dialogue plays in; required on a production_script/3 segment with any speaker line

place.description: where this plays, concrete (the back room of the club, night)

time.description: when, relative to the story (that night, an hour later)

present.description: cast ids physically in the scene; only they may speak or be spoken to (SC-04)

why_now.description: what just changed that forces this conversation NOW

pov.description: the cast id whose want drives the scene

want.description: the pov hero's short-term, concrete want in THIS scene

obstacle_want.description: the opposing want of another present character (SC-03: must differ from want)

value.description: the value at stake (control, trust, safety)

open_charge.description: the value's charge when the scene opens

close_charge.description: the charge when it closes; SC-02: must differ from open_charge or the scene is a nonevent

turn.description: the beat where the scene turns, in one sentence

exit.description: how the scene ends: a failure that sets a new goal, a success that costs, or an interruption

surface_topic.description: what the characters talk ABOUT on the surface (SC-10)

real_subject.description: what the scene is REALLY about; no line may state it verbatim (SC-10)

mode.description: the scene's conflict mode (DW-09: learner is one mode among several, varied across the episode)

drama.description: what this segment does in the story (ST rules): its function, how it follows the one before (but / therefore), the stakes, the value that turns, the loops it opens and closes

turn.description: ST-02: every segment after the first follows by BUT or THEREFORE, never AND THEN

stakes.description: what is lost if it goes wrong, in plain words

shift.description: the value that turns in this segment, as 'from -> to' (safe -> hunted)

claim_share.description: ST-09: what kind of statement carries this segment

job.description: what this beat does for the viewer (EPISODE_STANDARDS 5.4, PV-39)

feel.description: what the viewer should understand or feel at the end of the beat

rules.description: rulebook rules this beat must respect

speaker.description: cast id of the hero who speaks this line in their own voice (D-45, PV-32); absent = the narrator

to.description: kept when a Short reuses a scene line (SC-04); not checked on a Short's own lines

visual_beats.description: VB rules on a Short (SS-09): the visual beats of this line, same contract as a segment line's

style.description: SS-01: the Short's style; a set of 10 uses at least 6 styles

drama.description: the story layer (ST rules, docs/STORY_ENGINE.md): premise, the dramatic question, the hero arcs, the open loops and the set-ups the segments open and pay off

premise.description: the alternate reality in one sentence: what is changed, for whom

question.description: the dramatic question the whole video answers (ST-01)

promise.description: what the viewer gets by the end; the title and thumbnail make this promise

needs.description: the human needs the episode serves (ST-08); at least three

arcs.description: cast id -> want, need, flaw, change (ST-04)

file.description: an existing picture (relative to the script's picture folders)

engine.description: canva: filler pictures only (D-53, PV-43); made by hand in Canva, placed as a file

subject.description: who does what, with which feeling: written with the line it illustrates

refs.description: picture ids the reference painter starts from

costume.description: clothing words when the default (the visitors' era) is wrong for this picture

stand_in.description: draft only: an existing picture shown until this one is painted

tier.description: Gemini batch tier (D-52, imagegen/routing.py); default standard

tier_reason.description: premium only: why this picture needs the dearer model (PV-40)

beat.description: a visual beat (VB rules, docs/STORY_ENGINE.md): something new on screen, on a phrase of this line, written with the line

at.description: the words of THIS line the beat lands on

offset.description: seconds after the phrase's first word starts (never a clock time: the read decides)

why.description: what in the line at that instant this beat shows (VB-03)

pos.description: where on the frame (0..1); a label or highlight points at this spot of the picture

thing.description: prop: the object named in the line

asset.description: prop: a cut-out PNG (relative to the picture folders or the repo); without one the prop is drawn as a word sticker

claim.description: claim id behind a number on screen (invariant 5)

effect.description: accent: a camera accent of production/accents.py

who.description: expression: the cast id whose face changes (default: the line's speaker)

cue.description: VB-08: the short light sound that marks this beat (audio/cues.py), or 'none' with a reason

event.description: VB-08 (/3): the story event this cue marks; on /3 a cue without an event FAILs - silence is the default

why.description: why this sound (or why none: an effect already sounds here, a quiet expression)
